record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: What is the correct energy spectrum of axions emitted by the scaling axion-string network, and therefore how large is the string contribution to the present QCD-axion dark-matter abundance?

evidence.quote: What is currently of particular interest about the scaling solution is energy spectrum of emitted axions. There has been much theoretical and numerical work on this subject but it is currently unresolved, see e.g. Ref. [217] for a recent attempt. The spectrum of emitted axions is important because the number density of emitted axions is the string contribution to axion DM. The current results vary from saying that the string contribution is dominant to completely irrelevant. It would be interesting if more light could be shed on this debate.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the axion field arising as the angular (Nambu-Goldstone) mode of a complex scalar field that undergoes a global U(1) Peccei-Quinn symmetry breaking in an expanding (radiation-dominated, FRW) universe. After symmetry breaking, a network of global cosmic strings (axion strings) forms and is expected to evolve toward a scaling regime in which the average number of long strings per Hubble volume approaches an order-one (possibly logarithmically growing) constant. Throughout its evolution the network radiates massless axions; below the QCD scale the axion acquires a small mass m_a from QCD instantons, and the resulting cold axion population contributes to the present cold dark matter abundance.

Let dE/dk(k,t) denote the instantaneous differential energy spectrum (per unit comoving volume per unit comoving wavenumber k) of axions emitted by the scaling string network at cosmic time t, normalized so that the total radiated energy density equals the energy lost by the strings. Parametrize the spectrum, between an IR cutoff set by the Hubble scale H(t) and a UV cutoff set by the string-core scale ~m_r (the radial-mode mass), as
   dE/dk ∝ k^{-q}    for H(t) ≪ k ≪ m_r,
with a possibly time-dependent spectral index q = q(t), and let x_str denote the resulting fractional contribution of strings (and their decay products at the QCD epoch) to the present-day axion dark matter number density relative to the misalignment contribution.

Problem: Determine the correct shape of dE/dk(k,t) emitted by the scaling axion-string network — in particular, the value (and time dependence) of the spectral index q in the scaling regime — and use it to compute the resulting string contribution x_str to the present QCD-axion cold dark matter abundance.
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains actively debated but has seen substantial progress. Recent large-scale adaptive-mesh-refinement lattice simulations (2024–2025) argue for an essentially scale-invariant emission spectrum (q≈1) and predict the QCD axion mass in the window ~45–65 μeV, while other groups continue to find a logarithmically growing spectral index q>1 with enhanced IR emission. A consensus on the spectral index and the resulting string contribution to dark matter has not yet been reached, so the problem is best characterized as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Axion Mass Prediction from Adaptive Mesh Refinement Cosmological Lattice Simulations
status_evidence.snippet: Large-scale AMR simulations find a scale-invariant axion radiation spectrum to within 1% and predict m_a ∈ (45, 65) μeV.
status_evidence.claim: Recent simulations claim a nearly scale-invariant emission spectrum and a specific dark-matter mass window.

status_evidence.title: The spectrum of axions in a scaling string network
status_evidence.snippet: Studies spectra of all components of the axion current and their unequal time correlators from string networks.
status_evidence.claim: The spectral shape remains a subject of active study in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Spectrum of global string networks and the axion dark matter mass
status_evidence.snippet: Reports logarithmic growth of the spectral index q>1 of axion radiation from strings.
status_evidence.claim: Competing results favor q>1 with logarithmic growth, leading to a different DM abundance.

status_evidence.title: Axion Dark Matter from Cosmic String Network
status_evidence.snippet: Recent analysis of dark-matter contribution from the axion string network.
status_evidence.claim: The string contribution to axion DM continues to be reassessed.
